dedupe_keys.name: bgs britpits british pits database of mines and quarries

description: BritPits is the BGS database of surface and underground mineral workings in Great Britain, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands. It covers active, inactive, dormant and ceased mines, quarries, oil and gas wells, ash and desulphogypsum plants, and mineral handling sites such as wharfs and rail depots. Each record holds the site name, location, address, operator, mineral planning authority, geology, commodities produced and operational status; the GeoIndex description counts over 6,000 workings, about 2,000 of them active. Data come from BGS records, the Coal Authority, industry and the Valuation Office Agency, and active sites are updated with local authorities and industry. Version 4 was issued in February 2026 (DOI 10.5285/f6b41d3c-b881-4f3d-8e10-40dc7262de1a) and replaces version 3; the older Scottish quarries database has been merged into it. Access: the BGS page lists it as open and premium: the full dataset costs £56.78 per region (15 regions), the active, inactive and dormant layer £170.34 for Great Britain, subject to users and fees, while an index of active workings is free as a WMS layer and in the onshore GeoIndex viewer; format is GIS point data and database tables. Caveats: older operator details are incomplete, and copyright rests with NERC. For simulation it locates extraction sites that supply aggregates and industrial minerals, useful for material supply chain and hazard exposure studies. Related catalogue records include BGS Mining Hazard (not including coal) and the UK Minerals Yearbook.
licence: BGS licence (copyright NERC); index layer free to view
